## Scope and evidence level
Confirmed on `maestro/rebuild-fork-dev-clean` at **b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7**. Original compiled Atlas modules, real temporary Git repositories/filesystem, `composeRuntime().handler.handle('atlas-memory-emit', {entry})`, **real gitleaks 8.30.1**, Node 22.17.1. No substituted hashing, store, scanner or write gate. This is a local fault-recovery/data-loss case, not a claim of a production incident or remote exploit.

## Actual behavior
1. Successfully emit project rule A.
2. Model a torn final append by leaving an incomplete JSON fragment at the end of `.atlas/memory.jsonl`, **without a terminating newline**. The existing A is intact.
3. Emit a different, valid project rule B through the real governed handler.
4. Handler returns `ok:true`, `data.admitted:true` and B's record.
5. Reopen the store and runtime. Only A is readable; B is absent from `memoryRecall({owner:'alice'})`. Rejected-line count is still 1.

`appendFileSync` concatenates B's serialized event directly onto the unfinished fragment. The single malformed physical line now contains both the preexisting damaged suffix and the newly acknowledged event. Adding the final newline does not restore B as an independently parseable line.

### Controls actually executed
| Existing tail | B acknowledged | Readable records after reopen | Rejected lines |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Healthy, terminated | yes | 2 | 0 |
| Damaged, **terminated** | yes | 2 | 1 |
| Damaged, **unterminated** | yes | **1** | 1 |

The fault does not require large records or concurrent writers. Existing torn-line tests use a damaged fragment that already ends in `\n`; that does not exercise recovery from this state. A separate diagnostic asserts `acknowledged(B) => readable_after_reopen(B)` and exits 1 for the unterminated-tail case.

## Source trace
- [durable-log.ts](https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/adapter-io/src/durable-log.ts): `append` appends JSON + LF without checking/recovering the existing final boundary; `read` splits on LF.
- [memory-store.ts](https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/adapter-io/src/memory-store.ts): append delegates to that primitive.
- [memory-emit.ts](https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/adapter-io/src/memory-emit.ts): reads the log but ignores `rejected`, appends and acknowledges.
- [memory-store.test.ts](https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/adapter-io/test/memory-store.test.ts): existing malformed-tail fixture is newline-terminated.

Distinct from #19: that issue concerns preexisting corrupt **CAS objects**. This issue concerns framing of a subsequent append in the **memory JSONL log**.

## Required outcome
Either recover a safe record boundary under a documented concurrency protocol, or refuse the write explicitly before acknowledging admission. Do not silently truncate damaged evidence or rewrite intact prior records. A superficial unlocked last-byte check is not a complete concurrent-writer solution.

## Completeness criteria
Cover healthy tail, malformed terminated tail, malformed unterminated tail, valid JSON missing only its final LF, reopen, and competing appenders. Check both memory and Orientation consumers of the shared primitive.

## Success criteria
A successful governed write is independently readable after reopening. Damage is observable; a refused write is not reported as admitted. Existing good records remain unchanged.

## Quality standards
Regression uses original modules, temporary filesystem and real public handler, with explicit scanner boundary. No hardcoded pass or replacement kernel. Separate logical persistence from any untested power-loss durability claim.

## Definition of done
Commit the regression and fix; rerun relevant original memory/durable-log tests and handler/CLI readback. Record precise before/after evidence.

## Invariants
Acknowledged record implies readable record; preexisting intact records survive; incomplete data is never silently treated as healthy; retries and parallel writers preserve record boundaries.

## Audit artifacts
Round-2 probe: `memory-round2.mjs`; evidence: `memory-round2.json` cases `tail-clean`, `tail-damaged-terminated`, `tail-damaged-unterminated`. The accompanying documentation publication will link the exact probe and result commit; this issue records the already executed evidence, not an implementation fix.
title: [Atlas][P1] Memory emit acknowledges a record that becomes unreadable after an unterminated log tail

body:
## Scope and proof
Product SHA **b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7**. Exercised the original `composeRuntime` governed memory handler and reopened durable store, using real Git/filesystem and gitleaks 8.30.1; no fake store, kernel or scanner.

## Two observed consequences of the same accounting defect
**Exact replay:** a valid project rule of 300 whitespace-delimited words is admitted for actor `alice` (member cap = 500). Repeating the identical request is refused as `over-cap`, although the content-keyed durable fold has one record and the injected header still contains only 300 words. Control: an identical 250-word replay succeeds and still folds to one record.

**Historical versions:** emit one 100-word rule with stored frecency values 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, then 6. First five writes are admitted. The sixth is refused as `over-cap`; the current header contains **one rule, 100 words**, while the append-only history contains five versions. History that is deliberately retained now permanently spends the injection budget.

These are the product's own whitespace-token proxy, not measured model tokens. The defect remains even under that declared metric.

## Cause
[memory-emit.ts](https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/adapter-io/src/memory-emit.ts) passes **every historic owner/project entry plus the candidate** to `capGate`. It neither removes an exact idempotent replay nor constructs the post-write live projection.

[memory-read.ts](https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/adapter-io/src/memory-read.ts) instead uses latest-by-rule positions and effective-frecency/top-12 selection for the injected slab. Write accounting and served accounting therefore describe different sets.

[rules.ts](https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/memory/src/rules.ts) defines MEM-3 as the cap over the **injected project set**. [memory-store.ts](https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/adapter-io/src/memory-store.ts) separately documents content-idempotent append/fold.

## Expected behavior and design constraint
Calculate the cap using a precisely defined, shared post-write live/injected projection, while retaining the archive. Exact replay must not consume an additional budget allocation. Do not fix this by deleting history or disabling the cap. If a distinct archive-storage quota is desired, name and govern it separately rather than reporting it as an injection cap.

## Counterevidence / limits
A genuinely new oversized active rule should still be refused. The existing cap function correctly sums the input it receives; this is a **composition/set-selection defect**, not faulty arithmetic. No assertion here that arbitrary frecency updates are the final intended citation policy.

## Completeness criteria
Cover exact retries on both sides of half the cap; same-rule updates; rules evicted by age or capacity; separate owners; genuinely excessive post-write active set; restart; and serialized/concurrent write consistency.

## Success criteria
300-word exact retry succeeds without another logical record. Reaffirming a single 100-word live rule does not hit the 500-word injection limit solely because previous versions are retained. Genuine over-cap live state remains refused.

## Quality standards
Use original read and write doors over the same real durable store. Assert both history preservation and final injected size; never substitute a synthetic array for the served projection.

## Definition of done
Regression and shared accounting fix committed, original memory tests pass, public handler and CLI receipts/readback agree with the projected set.

## Invariants
History retention is not injection; replay does not spend new logical budget; cap remains enforced on its declared set; one owner's use does not spend another owner's budget.

## Evidence register
`memory-round2.mjs` / `memory-round2.json`: `retry-250`, `retry-300`, `archive-cap`. This round also ran the relevant original suite: 17 files, 158 tests passed. Those passes do not invalidate these additional failing scenarios.
title: [Atlas][P2] Project-memory cap counts retries and archived versions instead of the injected rule set

body:
## Scope / observed proof
Confirmed on **b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7**, with original compiled modules, real temporary Git repositories and filesystem, actor `orch`, original `composeRuntime` handler and **gitleaks 8.30.1**. Repeated in independent fixture sets. This is a validator-composition defect, not an authorization finding.

## Actual vs expected
The dedicated `validateLogbookEntry` rejects an over-cap or empty logbook prose section. The same entry is accepted and persisted through `atlas-memory-emit`.

| `shipped` section | Dedicated validator | Governed handler | Durable readback |
|---|---|---|---|
| 280 ASCII characters | valid | admitted | present |
| 281 ASCII characters | `section over cap: shipped` | **admitted** | **present** |
| empty string | `unfilled section: shipped` | **admitted** | **present** |
| whitespace-only string | `unfilled section: shipped` | **admitted** | **present** |

All other fields conform to the logbook template; each case uses a distinct PR identity. No field is omitted and no scanner result is mocked.

## Source trace
- [logbook.ts](https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/memory/src/logbook.ts): `LOGBOOK_SECTION_CAP = 280`; `validateLogbookEntry` requires the five prose sections to be filled and within the bound; `makeLogbookStore.append` consumes this validator.
- [template.ts](https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/memory/src/template.ts): `validate` checks field presence, allowed keys and field types. A string of 281 characters or an empty string passes this generic shape check.
- [memory-emit.ts](https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/adapter-io/src/memory-emit.ts): the durable door invokes only generic `validate(kind, entry)`; its logbook-specific stage checks author and duplicate PR, not `validateLogbookEntry`.

The two stores therefore do not enforce the same MEM-8 section discipline.

## Required outcome
Compose the dedicated logbook constraints into the durable governed door, with an explicit structured refusal before persistence. Reuse the authoritative validator rather than maintaining a second hardcoded cap. If the section discipline is intentionally being changed, reconcile the contract and both paths explicitly; do not leave divergent semantics.

## Completeness criteria
Test all five prose sections at 0, whitespace, 280 and 281 characters; valid surrounding fields; wrong field types; duplicate PR; non-orchestrator; and scanner failures. Record the intended ordering when multiple constraints fail.

## Success criteria
An entry rejected by the authoritative logbook section validator cannot be acknowledged or returned from durable logbook recall after a governed write. The boundary-valid control remains admitted.

## Quality standards
Real governed handler and readback; original validator reused; no weakening scanner or author checks. Keep char-count semantics explicit rather than conflating them with LLM token count.

## Definition of done
Regression and production composition change committed, original memory suites pass, CLI/MCP rejection remains named and attributable.

## Invariants
The stored logbook satisfies its section contract; rejected writes append nothing; valid entries remain readable; writer authorization and one-per-PR discipline remain unchanged.

## Evidence
Round-2 `memory-round2.mjs`, cases `logbook-valid`, `logbook-over`, `logbook-empty`, `logbook-blank`; recorded in both first and independent second result sets.
title: [Atlas][P2] Governed memory emit persists logbook sections rejected by the dedicated logbook validator

body:
## Scope / proof strength
Confirmed on **b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7** using the **original exported `replaceOwnTargets`**, two real Node subprocesses and actual filesystem renames on macOS. Three controlled interleavings reproduced the same result. A serial A-then-B control succeeds with both files at B.

The scheduler pauses writer A through the existing `operations.renameSync` seam **after executing the real rename**. No filesystem result is fabricated. This is a deterministic race schedule, not a claim about its uncontrolled frequency, full CLI validation, crash atomicity or power-loss durability.

## Observed schedule
Initially snapshot and skills both represent `old`.

1. A backs up both old targets and installs snapshot A, then pauses before installing skills A.
2. B runs the entire original replacement function against the same targets. It installs snapshot B and skills B, cleans its backups, and **returns success**.
3. Resume A. Its attempt to rename the nonempty skills directory onto B's nonempty directory fails with `ENOTEMPTY`.
4. A's rollback removes the **current snapshot B**, restores its own old snapshot, and then fails to restore old skills onto B's nonempty skills directory.
5. Final state: **snapshot = old; skills = B**. B had already returned success. A returns an error including the rollback failure.

All three subprocess trials produced this result. The serial control finishes `snapshot=B, skills=B`.

## Root cause
[materialize-own-snapshot.mjs — replaceOwnTargets](https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/scripts/materialize-own-snapshot.mjs): per-writer booleans such as `snapshotInstalled` are treated as ownership of the **currently named** target during rollback. Another writer can replace that target before rollback. Random temporary/backup names avoid scratch-name collision but do not serialize publication or prove ownership of the installed generation.

The file already disclaims crash atomicity across two paths; that disclaimer is not the issue here. Both processes stay alive and complete their error handling. This also differs from #31 (symlink entrypoint no-op).

## Impact and bounds
Concurrent refresh jobs can damage a successful publication and leave a mismatched pair. A later verification gate may correctly detect that mismatch; **this issue does not claim the verifier accepts it**. Backup contents can remain for manual recovery. The defect is cross-writer rollback ownership and publication consistency.

## Required outcome
Protect the whole replacement/rollback decision with a robust single-writer protocol, or publish immutable generations through one atomic authority pointer. A failing writer must never delete or restore over another writer's committed generation. Keep the existing honest crash-atomicity disclaimer unless separately proven otherwise.

## Completeness criteria
Serial replacement; failure at each rename; concurrent A/B schedules before and after each publication step; rollback failures; stale lock/recovery policy if locks are used; and reader consistency. Include the exact successful-B/failed-A schedule above.

## Success criteria
After B is acknowledged and A subsequently fails, B's snapshot and skills remain intact, or the protocol rejects/serializes the conflicting operation without publishing mismatched targets. Original serial rollback controls remain correct.

## Quality standards
Two real subprocesses, real filesystem, bounded deterministic barriers; no sleeps as the sole assertion of ordering; no fake successful rename. Keep publication tests separate from graph/source validation and crash tests.

## Definition of done
Regression and publication protocol fix committed, original materialization/rollback suite passes, repeated race cases preserve both targets and evidence explains recovery behavior.

## Invariants
Rollback may undo only state still owned by its transaction; an acknowledged generation cannot be overwritten by an unrelated failed rollback; snapshot and skills never masquerade as one consistent generation when mismatched.

## Evidence
Round-2 `own-replacement-race.mjs` and `own-replacement-race.json`: one serial control and three real two-process interleavings. The desired-invariant run exits 1 on the current product.
title: [Own][P1] A failed materializer rollback can overwrite another writer's completed publication

body:
## Classification / scope
**Integration gap against the proposed Static Own protocol**, with observed host behavior on **b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7**. Do not describe the entire proposed protocol as already shipped, or this as a demonstrated unauthorized execution.

The test runs the original Own CLI materializer, original freshness verifier, real host `ToolRegistry`/`SkillTool`, real Git repository and real source files. Tool permission is accepted by the fixture, as in the existing host skill tests. No real LLM or governed Task execution is involved.

## Observed behavior
1. Create and commit `src/a.ts` exporting `value = 1` in an isolated Git fixture.
2. Produce an Own skill with the **original `materialize-own-snapshot.mjs`** from a reviewed fixture snapshot whose revision and source blob match that commit. This runs the actual CLI's revision/source checks; the receipt is not a fabricated Markdown imitation.
3. `verifyStaticOwnFreshness` returns `READY` and the real host skill tool serves it. This is the positive control.
4. Change `src/a.ts` to `value = 2`, without refreshing Own.
5. The original freshness verifier now returns `HOLD`, stale source `src/a.ts`.
6. The original host skill tool still returns `Loaded skill: own_c3Jj` with the claim that the fixture exports `value = 1`.

Both **cold loading after the source has already changed** and **reusing a loaded skill after the source changes** reproduce this. Therefore, invalidating the skill cache alone would not close the gap.

Actual diagnostic: 3 scenarios, fresh control passes; stale-cold and stale-warm fail the desired invariant that held ownership content is not injected as current. Results are in `host-own.json`.

## Source trace / contract
- [Static Own protocol](https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/specs/hugr-maestro/own-protocol.md): proposed primary context path; missing/stale/ambiguous/held ownership must hold.
- [Maestro prompt](https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/packages/opencode/src/agent/prompt/maestro.txt): instructs the model to load current `own_*` skills and not replace stale ownership via generic search.
- [skill/index.ts](https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/packages/opencode/src/skill/index.ts): generic discovery parses frontmatter and stores text; `require` returns the named entry.
- [tool/skill.ts](https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/packages/opencode/src/tool/skill.ts): returns that content without an Own-specific freshness/canonical-artifact validation step.
- [own-artifact.ts](https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/retrieval/src/own-artifact.ts): the existing freshness function correctly detects the source change in the same fixture.

## Required outcome
Connect a deliberately scoped Own availability/validation boundary to the ownership-consumption path. Do not impose Own receipts on unrelated ordinary skills. A stale artifact should produce an attributable hold and refresh worklist, not merely rely on a prompt asking the model to recognize stale content it has no verified status for.

Freshness is not full semantic truth or complete graph coverage; preserve those separate meanings and do not claim this one integration closes #29.

## Completeness criteria
Valid artifact; changed or removed source; cold and warm loading; missing receipt; noncanonical name/path; duplicates; coverage/pointer dependencies; revision/worktree change; and ordinary non-Own skill compatibility. Identify every host entrypoint that consumes ownership text, including any mention-based path.

## Success criteria
The tested stale-cold and stale-warm cases return a structured hold before stale Own content is presented as current. The fresh control and normal skills still load. Status binds the exact content and source view that are delivered.

## Quality standards
Use the original materializer and host tool; no mocked freshness verdict. Keep permission tests, proof of semantic claims, and full governed execution separate from this bounded integration test.

## Definition of done
Implement and document the actual ownership-consumption boundary; add host integration regressions; rerun Maestro and skill suites; update the proposed/shipped status only to the extent actually demonstrated.

## Invariants
A prompt is not a freshness verifier; cache invalidation is not validation; held ownership is not injected as current; the bytes validated are the bytes consumed.

## Evidence
`audit-round2-own.test.ts`, `host-own.json`, `host-own.log`. The preceding source revision and blob were real Git values generated per fixture; no paid model request was made.
title: [Maestro/Own][P2] Host skill loading serves stale static Own artifacts despite the freshness contract returning HOLD

body:
## Scope and qualification
Confirmed on **b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7** by calling original `createDurableOrientation` / `orientEvent` over real files and reopening the store. This is an **adapter/model correctness issue**. The composed runtime reads Orientation, but this audit did **not** find a production automatic writer driving `append`; do not describe a complete live orchestration state cycle as exercised.

## Reproduction and actual result
Use valid causal references, not independent unlabeled appends:

1. Append state `running`; retain its event identity A.
2. Append state `blocked`, with `supersedes: [A]`; retain B.
3. Append state `running`, with `supersedes: [B]`.
4. Reopen and derive Orientation.

Expected current state: `running` (the third event is a new transition with a different parent).

Actual: **`blocked`**, with 3 physical JSONL records, only 2 logical events, and 0 rejected lines. Reproduced again in independent fixtures.

Control: `running -> blocked -> complete`, with equivalent supersedes references, produces `complete` correctly.

## Cause
[orient.ts](https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/memory/src/orient.ts) sets both `id` and `contentHash` from only `{channel, label}`. The third event has the **same identity as the first**, even though its `supersedes` describes a different causal occurrence.

[orientation-store.ts](https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/adapter-io/src/orientation-store.ts) appends it through the shared durable log with payload-keyed verification.

[durable-log.ts](https://github.com/gmhelmold/HuGR-Orchestra/blob/b0c33d2f6567a2c741240f3c44bc00ca2f01e7e7/foundation/atlas/packages/adapter-io/src/durable-log.ts) folds duplicate identities first-seen-wins. The recurrence is indistinguishable from a replay, so the third event's new parent is lost. B still supersedes the retained A.

This is not the separately documented narrower envelope-integrity guarantee: the test performs **only legitimate adapter appends**, with no hand editing or rehashing of events.

## Required outcome
Distinguish a repeated delivery of the same causal event from a new occurrence carrying the same human-readable label. Include sufficient causal identity and make supersedes/head resolution consistent with it. Do not add nondeterministic timestamps or random IDs merely to defeat deduplication; retain explicit retry semantics and deterministic folding. Existing persisted-log compatibility requires an explicit migration/version decision.

## Completeness criteria
State A->B->A; milestone recurrence where supported; exact retry of the same event; restart; merged/reordered logs; forked causal heads; malformed/missing parent references; and compatibility with existing payload-keyed Orientation logs.

## Success criteria
The causal cycle `running -> blocked -> running` derives the final state after reopening. Exact retry remains logically idempotent. The different-label control and current Orientation read entrypoints remain correct.

## Quality standards
Real adapter, kernel and durable fold; no replacement hashing or state evaluator. Separate this proven adapter behavior from any unimplemented automatic event writer and from confidentiality/authentication properties.

## Definition of done
Regression and event-identity/lineage change committed with a storage-compatibility plan, relevant original Orientation/kernel tests pass, runtime readback documented.

## Invariants
Event identity distinguishes causal occurrence from label value; exact delivery replay is idempotent; recurrence is not discarded; derived state follows the supersession graph rather than the first occurrence of a string.

## Evidence
Round-2 `memory-round2.mjs` / first and second result files: `orientation-complete` and `orientation-running`. Existing original Orientation tests passed; their append-concurrency case uses distinct labels and does not exercise recurrence.
title: [Atlas][P2] Orientation event identity cannot represent a legitimate return to an earlier state label
